differences.what: the corner block at the south-west corner, with its narrow cant, carried up a storey past the cornice as a square tower under a tall slated hip with a crested top and two finials (x 610-1135 px, y 80-1600). T-3175 measured it against the 1911 sheet: the photograph's turned square reads a face about 4-4.7 m across (its broad south-west face x 860-1130 px, its narrow north-west face x 820-860, at the scale of the cornice and storeys), where the sheet's bump is a square of about 2.4 m on a face centred on the main block's corner; through this camera a tower of the photograph's size would stand about 2.8 m out of the front, and no camera fitted to the sheet's plan holds both (the best leaves about 165 px). The camera itself misses the pavilion's north edge by about 90 px (x 371 against the print's 277). T-3176 owns the reconciliation, the re-solve and the tower

the pavilion's steep pyramidal roof over the cornice, with its finial and its triple attic lights (x 330-560 px, y 350-830); the render showed the pavilion's low hip under the main mansard. T-3175 carries the pavilion up an attic storey from the main eave to its own cornice at the main curb's height (y about 605 px, 16.8 m), three tall lights in its wall, under a slated crown hipped on every side at 47 degrees to a point (about 20.5 m) and a turned iron finial
the rear part's step out on the south flank (the sheet's 1.6 m at u 0-14.6), seen past the corner at x 1080-1150 px
the carved hoods over the pavilion's lights and the segmental hoods over the window bay's (plain lintels stand in)
the alternating light and dark stone courses of the front and flank
the porch's round arches and its steps rising along the front from the north (a flight stands across the porch's width)
the barred basement lights' full height, about 1.5 m (K02's two base courses hold them to 0.75 m)
the window heights and places on the front and in the pavilion, read through the camera
